spatial_claims.claim: Points lie in order A, C, D, B on line AB, with AC = CB (C is the midpoint)
CB = CD + DB, segment decomposition from ordering C, D, B
CB = CD + DB used again to distribute R(CB, CD) via Prop 2.1
AD = AC + CD, segment decomposition from ordering A, C, D
AC = CB substituted into R(AD, DB) decomposition

configuration_map: All points are collinear on line AB with ordering A--C--D--B. C is the midpoint of AB (AC = CB). D lies between C and B. Segments decompose as: AB = AC + CD + DB, CB = CD + DB, AD = AC + CD. No 2D or 3D geometric constructions are made; the entire proof operates on segment relationships along a single line, using Proposition 2.1 (rectangle distribution / distributive property) to manipulate rectangle and square areas algebraically.
pass_reason: The proof is purely algebraic, using Proposition 2.1 (distributive property of rectangles) applied to segments on a single line. The only spatial claims concern collinear point ordering (A, C, D, B) and segment addition, all of which are mutually consistent. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no 2D configuration issues arise.
